/-!
# Ringel's Conjecture

*Reference:* G. Ringel, *Problem 25*, in *Theory of Graphs and its Applications*
(Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963), Academia, Prague, 1964.

Ringel's conjecture (1963): the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into copies of any tree
with $n$ edges. It remains open; the case of all sufficiently large $n$ is proved by
Montgomery–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov, see `Arxiv/2001.02665/RingelConjecture.lean`.
-/

@[expose] public section
namespace RingelConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
For any tree $T$ with $n$ edges, the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into
$2n+1$ edge-disjoint copies of $T$.

A "copy" of $T$ is the image $T.\text{map}(f_i)$ of $T$ under a vertex embedding
$f_i : V \hookrightarrow \text{Fin}(2n+1)$; the copies are pairwise edge-disjoint
and together cover every edge of $K_{2n+1}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem ringel_conjecture {V : Type} [Finite V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) (hT : T.IsTree)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : T.edgeSet.ncard = n) :
    ∃ f : Fin (2 * n + 1) → (V ↪ Fin (2 * n + 1)),
      Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (T.map (f i)).edgeSet (T.map (f j)).edgeSet) ∧
      ⨆ i, T.map (f i) = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end RingelConjecture

reformulations.difference: The source describes an edge partition into subgraphs isomorphic to T. Lean instead uses injective vertex maps, pairwise-disjoint image edge sets, and a graph supremum equal to the complete graph. Each mapped graph formally retains unused ambient vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given an embedding f, take the subgraph with vertex set range(f) and adjacency T.map f. This subgraph is isomorphic to T and has exactly the mapped edge set. Conversely, compose an isomorphism onto a subgraph with its vertex inclusion to obtain the required embedding and the same edge set. The edge set of the graph supremum is the union of the edge sets. A generic equivalence between these two decomposition formulations was proved in /workspace/review/copy_equivalence.lean, without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: R. Montgomery, A. Pokrovskiy and B. Sudakov, A proof of Ringel's Conjecture, arXiv:2001.02665; LaTeX source, especially the abstract, Introduction, Conjecture 1.1, Theorem 1.2, concluding remarks and bibliography: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2001.02665
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling — discussion of Ringel's conjecture and its partial resolution.

review.notes: No mathematical defect or status discrepancy found. Finite V ensures that edgeSet.ncard is an ordinary finite edge count, and IsTree excludes the empty vertex type. Independently proved the full zero-edge case and checked a concrete one-edge decomposition of K3 in /workspace/review/checks.lean. The cited paper proves only the sufficiently-large-n case, consistent with the all-n statement's research-open tag. The original proceedings scan required authorization; source verification used its explicit restatement as Conjecture 1.1 in the cited paper.
